title: Sanierung Mehrfamilienhaus - Kopernikusring 1-9, 36-44 16227 Eberswalde, Deutschland, Fassadenarbeiten
description: Das Bauvorhaben umfasst die Sanierung und Modernisierung der bestehenden Mehrfamilienhäuser. Die Gebäude stammen aus dem Jahr 1973 und umfassen insgesamt ca. 180 Wohneinheiten mit einer Gesamtwohnfläche von ca. 10.967 m². Der Wohnungsbestand ist überwiegend vermietet; eine Teilsanierung erfolgte im Jahr 1994. Weitere Leerwohnungsinstandsetzungen finden seit dem Jahr 2025 statt und sind bei der Abstimmung der Schnittstellen zu berücksichtigen. Die zu vergebenden Leistungen betreffen die Instandsetzung und malermäßige Überarbeitung der bestehenden Fassaden einschließlich der zugehörigen Untergrundvorbereitungs-, Schutz-, Anschluss- und Nebenarbeiten. Die vorhandenen Außenwände bestehen gemäß Modernisierungskonzept aus ca. 29 cm Leichtbeton und einem bestehenden Wärmedämmverbundsystem mit ca. 8 cm EPS-Dämmung einschließlich Armierungsschicht und Oberputz. Das vorhandene Wärmedämmverbundsystem soll grundsätzlich erhalten und in schadhaften Bereichen örtlich instand gesetzt bzw. teilweise erneuert werden. Eine vollflächige Erneuerung oder Aufdopplung der Fassadendämmung ist im Modernisierungskonzept nicht vorgesehen. Die Arbeiten erfolgen überwiegend im bewohnten Bestand. Der Schutz der Bewohner, die Nutzbarkeit der erforderlichen Gebäudezugänge sowie der Schutz vorhandener und bereits erneuerter Bauteile sind zu berücksichtigen. Fördervorbehalt BEG EM, aufschiebende Bedingung Die ausgeschriebenen Leistungen sind Gegenstand einer beantragten Förderung nach BEG EM. Der Vertrag wird mit Zuschlag geschlossen; die Lieferungs- und Leistungspflichten stehen unter der aufschiebenden Bedingung der Förderzusage. Sie werden erst und nur insoweit wirksam, wie die beantragte Förderung durch die zuständige Förderstelle bewilligt wird. Der Auftraggeber informiert den Auftragnehmer über den Eintritt der Bedingung unverzüglich in Textform. Bis dahin bestehen keine Ausführungs-, Beschaffungs-, Vorhalte- oder sonstigen kostenverursachenden Leistungspflichten des Auftragnehmers. Wird die Förderung abgelehnt oder tritt die Bedingung nicht bis zum 01.03.2027 ein, entfällt die Verpflichtung zur Ausführung der betroffenen Leistungen. Ausführungsfristen beginnen erst mit Eintritt der Bedingung; weitergehende Ansprüche wegen des Nichteintritts sind ausgeschlossen.

title: Integrated Correctional program Model (ICPM) Program
description: An advanced contract award notice (ACAN) is a public notice indicating to the supplier community that a department or agency intends to award a contract for goods, services or construction to a pre-identified supplier, thereby allowing other suppliers to signal their interest in bidding, by submitting a statement of capabilities. If no supplier submits a statement of capabilities that meets the requirements set out in the ACAN, on or before the closing date and time stated in the ACAN, the contracting officer may then proceed with the award to the pre-identified supplier. 1. Definition of the requirement: Policy on Reciprocal Procurement: the Policy on Reciprocal Procurement does not apply to this procurement. The Correctional Service of Canada has a requirement for the delivery of programs to offenders. The main goal of maintenance is to review and refine core self management skills and apply them to real-life situations, obstacles, and high-risk situations to reduce risk to re-offend. One Integrated Correctional program Model (ICPM) program cycle is delivered at a rate of one session per week for 12 weeks on a continuous intake basis. The work will involve the following: 1.1 Objectives: To deliver ICPM to offenders. 1.2 Tasks: The Contractor’s facilitator must: a) Obtains CSC’s Certification through the Quality Review process. b) Provide delivery of the requested number of ICPM sessions to offenders referred by CSC, depending upon the need and according to national directives, policy and guidelines to a maximum of 10 offenders; c) Adhere to the course content by delivering program sessions for the ICPM Community Maintenance Programs in accordance with the program manual. d) Provide classroom space, program equipment and supplies, and all administrative services associated with the project; e) For all offenders who meet the criteria for enrollment to the ICPM Maintenance (MT) - the facilitator(s) must: • conduct file review; • complete pre-program semi-structured interview and interview booklet, return interview booklet to CSC; • complete Pre and Post program testing and assessment interviews and enter the information into Offender Management System (OMS) under Generic Program Performance Measure (GPPM) Screen within the first two sessions; • ensure offenders understanding and signing (or refusal to sign) of program consent form prior to program commencement while documenting such in a casework record in OMS. The consent to participate form must be placed on the Education and Training File; • prepare offender progress reports following the ICPM report template and enter the report into OMS at the completion of the required number of sessions; • forward all reports for review and approval by the Departmental Representative; • review the report with the participant and document same in casework record; • return interview booklets to CSC f) As per most recent Commissioner's Directive 726 - Correctional Programs, the facilitator must complete a casework record in OMS (unless at a site where there is no connectivity) within 1 working day: • when there is an offender contact which is not a requirement of the program, • an individual interview is completed with the offender, • a make-up session has been completed, • there is sharing of information regarding offender participation in the program, • after every session during the offenders’ cycle, • if there is significant information for the Case Management Team. Significant information would include but is not limited to the following: Breach of a condition, new offence, harm to self, harm to others, personal problems that impact risk. g) Each session must follow the same process (see below), be 2 hours in duration and includes a break of up to 15 minutes: • Roundtable and introductions (30 minutes) • Structured segment, each focusing on a specific theme and skills set (50 - 60 minutes) • Alternate Session – An alternate session may be offered in place of a structured segment session based on the identified needs of the participants present for that session, provided that the session is selected from pre-established topics within the program manual (PG 60 in ICPM Manual). • Update Self-Management Plan (10 minutes) • Wrap-up (5 - 10 minutes) h) Programs are to be delivered Monday to Friday in the evenings between 6pm-8pm. 1.3 Training Requirements The Contractor must participate in CSC-funded ICPM program delivery training when required and made available by CSC. • Training is delivered in person by CSC at the Correctional Learning and Development Centre in Moncton, New Brunswick. • Training dates are established by CSC based on operational requirements and the number of referrals identified by the Project Authority. • Initial training for CMP-MT consists of: o 10 business days of initial program delivery training; o 2 days of Indigenous Social History training; and o 7.5 hours of Generic Program Performance Measure (GPPM) training delivered over 2 days. • The Contractor must also attend refresher training when significant changes are made to the program model or when requested by the Project Authority. • The Contractor will be reimbursed for authorized travel costs associated with training. • The Contractor will not be compensated for time spent attending training. 1.4 Performance standards: Delivery of the ICPM: Community Maintenance Programs must be provided in accordance with the following documents: • Correctional Programs (CD 726); • National Correctional Program Standards (CD 726-1); • ICPM: Program Implementation and Program Management Guidelines • Commissioner’s Directives available at: • English: http://www.csc-s.gc.ca/text/legislat_e.shtml • French: http://www.csc-scc.gc.ca/text/legislat_f.shtml • ICPM Community Maintenance Program (Multi Target) Manuals - when connected to OMS; 1.5 Paper consumption: a. Should printed material be required, double sided printing in black and white format is the default unless otherwise specified by the Project Authority. b. The Contractor must ensure printed material is on paper with a minimum recycled content of 30% and/or certified as originating from a sustainably managed forest. c. The Contractor must recycle unneeded printed documents (in accordance with Security Requirements). 1.6 Constraints: 1.6.1 Location of work: a. The Contractor must perform the work at either the Contractor’s place of business or a location determined by the Contractor. b. Travel i. The Contractor will be required to travel to attend trainings as requested by the Project Authority. 1.6.2 Language of Work: The contractor must perform all work in English. 1.6.3 Security Requirements: This contract includes the following security requirements: IT Security Requirements Technical Document, to be included in the contract; and SECURITY REQUIREMENT FOR CANADIAN SUPPLIER: PWGSC FILE No. 21280-26-5322937 – Revision 1 1. The Contractor must, at all times during the performance of the Contract, hold a valid Designated Organization Screening (DOS), and obtain approved Document Safeguarding Capability at the level of PROTECTED B, issued by the Contract Security Program (CSP), Public Works and Government Services Canada (PWGSC). 2. The Contractor personnel requiring access to PROTECTED information, assets, or sensitive site(s) must EACH hold a valid RELIABILITY STATUS, granted or approved by the CSP, PWGSC. 3. The Contractor MUST NOT utilize its facilities to process, produce, or store PROTECTED information or assets until the CSP, PWGSC has issued written approval. 4. The Contractor MUST NOT utilize its Information Technology systems to electronically process, produce, or store PROTECTED information until the CSP, PWGSC has issued written approval. After approval has been granted or approved, these tasks may be performed at the level of PROTECTED B, including an IT Link at the level of PROTECTED B. 5. title: Purchase of two (2) Millimetre-Wave Frequency Extender Modules for a Vector Network Analyzers (VNAs) from 110 GHz to 170 GHz
description: NRC Herzberg Astronomy and Astrophysics (HAA) requires extended measurement capabilities in the millimetre-wave frequency range to support ongoing research in characterizing front-end components for low-noise receivers in radio astronomy. Existing Vector Network Analyzers (VNAs) at NRC HAA are currently limited to a maximum operational frequency of 116 GHz. To increase its measurement capability, NRC HAA intends to acquire frequency extender modules covering the 110–170 GHz band. These extenders must integrate with either of HAA's existing analysers (Keysight PNA N5227B and Rohde & Schwarz ZNA67), providing high dynamic range and stable two-port measurements.

If no other supplier submits a statement of capabilities demonstrating how they meet the set requirements in the ACAN by the closing date stated in the ACAN, the buyer may then proceed with the award to the pre-identified supplier. 2. Purpose of the ACAN Venue and Related Services for an International Conference 3. Requirement description Fisheries and Oceans Canada (DFO) has a requirement for a conference venue and associated venue services to host the 12th Our Ocean Conference (OOC12). The venue must support plenary programming, simultaneous side events, bilateral and VIP meetings, media activities, exhibitions, meals and networking, refreshments during registration and dedicated program breaks (e.g., coffee, small bites), and professional event production in a secure, accessible and operationally coherent setting. The venue must be available from May 9th to 11th, 2027, including activities planned for May 9th (e.g. opening reception, Youth Leadership Summit, possible side events, possible Ministerial or VIP meetings) and main conference programming on May 10th and 11, 2027. The Contractor must provide exclusive or appropriately controlled access to the required venue spaces, furniture, utilities, base building services and venue coordination for the conference period, including agreed setup, testing, event and teardown periods. The Contractor shall act as the prime contractor for all venue-related services, including venue rental, catering, registration and accreditation support, security services, audiovisual services, event production, event planning, staging, show management, exhibition services and associated conference delivery requirements. The Contractor may engage subcontractors; however, the Contractor remains fully responsible for the management, coordination and performance of all subcontracted services. If other potential suppliers submit a statement of capabilities during the 15 calendar days posting period that meet the requirements set out in the ACAN, DFO will proceed to a full-tendering process on whether the government's electronic tendering service or through traditional means, in order to award the Contract. If no other supplier submits on or before the closing date, a statement of capabilities meeting the requirements set out in the ACAN, a Contract will be awarded to the pre-selected supplier. 4. Evaluation criteria for assessment of statement of capabilities (minimum essential requirements) Any interested supplier must demonstrate by way of a statement of capabilities that it meets the following requirements: 4.1 A conference venue within the Halifax Regional Municipality available from May 9th to 11th, 2027, including setup, testing and teardown periods, capable of hosting an international conference of approximately 2,500 participants. 4.2 A plenary facility capable of accommodating at least 2,500 participants simultaneously, together with the infrastructure required to support professional event production, audiovisual services and livestreaming. 4.3 Within the same venue complex, a minimum of: a. a minimum of six (6) concurrent breakout or side-event rooms, each capable of accommodating at least 50 participants; b. a minimum of ten (10) private bilateral meeting rooms, each capable of accommodating at least 10 participants; c. one (1) secure meeting room for approximately 100 participants; and d. dedicated space for registration and accreditation, media operations, VIP functions, conference management, security operations, exhibitions, networking and delegate catering. 4.4 The capacity to provide or coordinate catering and refreshment services for approximately 2,500 attendees throughout a multi-day conference, including receptions, meals and scheduled program breaks. 4.5 The capability to act as the prime contractor responsible for the management and coordination of all venue-related services, including venue operations, catering, audiovisual services, event production, registration support, security services and exhibition services, whether delivered directly or through subcontractors. 4.6 A secure operating environment suitable for ministers, senior government officials, international delegations and VIP participants, with controlled access to conference spaces and the ability to support security operations. 4.7 A venue location within walking distance of sufficient hotel accommodation capacity to support conference delegates, officials and VIP participants. 5. Trade Agreements The requirement is subject to the following Trade Agreements: Canadian Free Trade Agreement (CFTA); Canada-Chile Free Trade Agreement (CCFTA); Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP) Canada-Colombia Free Trade Agreement; Canada-European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) Canada-Honduras Free Trade Agreement; Canada-Korea Free Trade Agreement; Canada-Panama Free Trade Agreement; Canada-Peru Free Trade Agreement; Canada-Ukraine Free Trade Agreement; Canada-United Kingdom Trade Continuity Agreement; World Trade Organization-Agreement on Government Procurement (WTO-GPA) 6. Justification for the pre-identified Supplier The pre-identified supplier is the only supplier that we are aware of who offers a product which meets all the Minimum Essential Requirements listed above. 7. Government Contract Regulations exception(s) The following exception(s) to the Government Contracts Regulations is (are) invoked for this procurement under subsection 6(d) – “only one person is capable of performing the work.” 8. Contract Period The Contract period will be from award to May 11, 2027 inclusive. 9. Estimated Cost The estimated value of the Contract is 3,200,000.00 $ CAD (excluding applicable taxes). 10. Name and Address of the Proposed Contractor Halifax Convention Centre (HCC) 1650 Argyle St. Halifax NS B3J 0E6 11. Suppliers’ right to submit a statement of capabilities Suppliers who consider themselves fully qualified and available to provide the services/goods described herein, may submit a Statement of Capabilities in writing, by e-mail, to the contact person identified in this Notice on or before the closing date and time of this Notice. The Statement of Capabilities must clearly demonstrate how the supplier meets the advertised requirements. 12. Closing Date The closing date for a submission of a Statement of Capabilities is November 25, 2026 at 2:00 p.m. EST. 13. title: Calcium Trisodium Pentetate (Ca-DTPA) ampoules
description: NOTICE OF PROPOSED PROCUREMENT The Department of National Defence (DND), through the Strategic Medical Countermeasures Program (SMCP) on behalf of the Canadian Forces Health Services Group (CF H Svcs Gp), has a requirement for the supply of Calcium Trisodium Pentetate (Ca-DTPA) ampoules for the treatment of Canadian Armed Forces (CAF) personnel who may have been exposed to radioactive contamination involving transuranic elements. The Ca-DTPA product must consist of sterile Calcium Trisodium Pentetate solution for injection, containing approximately 1,000 mg to 1,055 mg of active ingredient in a 5 mL ampoule suitable for intravenous administration. The product is intended for use as a medical countermeasure to enhance the elimination of internally deposited radioactive transuranic elements, including plutonium, americium and curium, following confirmed or suspected radiological exposure. The product must meet all applicable regulatory, quality assurance, packaging, labelling and shelf-life requirements specified in the solicitation documents. The initial requirement consists of the supply of 250 Ca-DTPA ampoules for delivery no later than 1 March 2027. The resulting contract is anticipated to be valid from contract award date to 31 March 2031 and includes additional scheduled deliveries of 250 ampoules in Fiscal Year 2027-2028 and 250 ampoules in Fiscal Year 2028-2029. The contract will also include an option for up to an additional 500 ampoules exercisable during the contract period. This procurement will be conducted through an Advance Contract Award Notice (ACAN). The Government of Canada has identified Heyl Chemisch-pharmazeutische Fabrik GmbH & Co. KG as the only supplier currently known to satisfy the operational, clinical and technical requirements associated with this requirement. Suppliers that consider themselves fully qualified and capable of meeting the complete requirement may submit a Statement of Capabilities during the posting period. The Crown retains the rights to negotiate with suppliers on any procurement. Documents may be submitted in either official language of Canada. Barring any applicable trade agreement exceptions or other legal restrictions, eligible suppliers may participate in this solicitation process. NOTE TO SUPPLIERS: Procurement Assistance Canada offers seminars to businesses interested in learning how to sell goods and services to the Government of Canada. These seminars are provided free of charge.

description: Arkkitehtuurikutsukilpailu: Hämeen ammattikorkeakoulun keskustakampus Hämeen ammattikorkeakoulu (HAMK) järjestää Hämeenlinnan Hämeensaaren uuden keskustakampuksen suunnittelusta arkkitehtuurikutsukilpailun yhteistyössä Hämeenlinnan kaupungin ja Suomen Arkkitehtiliitto SAFA:n kanssa. Kilpailutehtävänä on suunnitella arkkitehtonisesti korkeatasoinen ja toiminnallinen uusi keskustakampuskokonaisuus, joka palvelee HAMKia, sekä hämeenlinnalaisia. Uudisrakentamisen määrä on hankkeen ensimmäisen vaiheen kokonaan toteuduttua arviolta 12 000 hym². Kilpailussa tutkitaan kampusrakennuksen ja sen piharatkaisun liittymistä kaupunkirakenteeseen, Vanajaveden rantaan, julkisiin ulkotiloihin, liikenneverkkoon ja ympäröivään keskustaan. Hankkeessa haetaan pontta alueen kehittämisen käynnistymiselle huomioiden kytkeytyminen Hämeenlinnan keskustaan. Suunnittelukilpailun voittajan kanssa voidaan tehdä palveluhankintasopimus hankkeen asemakaavan kehittämisestä ja myöhemmästä jatko- ja toteutussuunnittelusta. Hankkeen lopullisen toteutumisen edellytyksenä on lainvoimainen asemakaava ja rahoituksen varmistuminen. Kilpailu on kaksivaiheinen niin, että ensimmäisessä vaiheessa pyydetään kaikilta halukkailta osallistujilta osallistumishakemukset. Osallistumishakemukset arvioidaan osallistumispyynnöllä esitettyjen vertailukriteereiden mukaisesti ja viisi (5) parasta kelpoisuusvaatimukset täyttävää hakijaa valitaan toiseen vaiheeseen varsinaiseen suunnittelukilpailuun. Viidelle valitulle kilpailijalle maksetaan kullekin 15 000 euroa (+alv) kilpailuohjelman mukaisesta määräajassa palautetusta kilpailutyöstä. Palkkiot maksetaan Suomen Arkkitehtiliiton kautta ja SAFA perii 7 % palkinnoista kilpailusääntöjensä mukaisesti. Kilpailun tarkemmat tiedot ja aikataulu on esitetty osallistumispyynnön liitteenä olevassa kilpailuohjelman luonnoksessa.,

title: Alkolukkojen ja niiden asennus-, huolto- ja kalibrointipalvelujen hankinta
description: Alkolukkojen ja niiden asennus-, huolto- ja kalibrointipalvelujen hankinta Hankinnan kohteena on ajoneuvoihin asennettavat alkolukot ja niiden vaihdettavat suukappaleet sekä alkolukkoihin liittyvät palvelut kuten asennus-, kalibrointi- ja huoltopalvelut. title: Finland – Organisation of architectural design contests – Arkkitehtuurikutsukilpailu: Hämeen ammattikorkeakoulun keskustakampus
description: Hämeen ammattikorkeakoulu (HAMK) järjestää Hämeenlinnan Hämeensaaren uuden keskustakampuksen suunnittelusta arkkitehtuurikutsukilpailun yhteistyössä Hämeenlinnan kaupungin ja Suomen Arkkitehtiliitto SAFA:n kanssa. Kilpailutehtävänä on suunnitella arkkitehtonisesti korkeatasoinen ja toiminnallinen uusi keskustakampuskokonaisuus, joka palvelee HAMKia, sekä hämeenlinnalaisia. Uudisrakentamisen määrä on hankkeen ensimmäisen vaiheen kokonaan toteuduttua arviolta 12 000 hym². Kilpailussa tutkitaan kampusrakennuksen ja sen piharatkaisun liittymistä kaupunkirakenteeseen, Vanajaveden rantaan, julkisiin ulkotiloihin, liikenneverkkoon ja ympäröivään keskustaan. Hankkeessa haetaan pontta alueen kehittämisen käynnistymiselle huomioiden kytkeytyminen Hämeenlinnan keskustaan. Suunnittelukilpailun voittajan kanssa voidaan tehdä palveluhankintasopimus hankkeen asemakaavan kehittämisestä ja myöhemmästä jatko- ja toteutussuunnittelusta. Hankkeen lopullisen toteutumisen edellytyksenä on lainvoimainen asemakaava ja rahoituksen varmistuminen. Kilpailu on kaksivaiheinen niin, että ensimmäisessä vaiheessa pyydetään kaikilta halukkailta osallistujilta osallistumishakemukset. Osallistumishakemukset arvioidaan osallistumispyynnöllä esitettyjen vertailukriteereiden mukaisesti ja viisi (5) parasta kelpoisuusvaatimukset täyttävää hakijaa valitaan toiseen vaiheeseen varsinaiseen suunnittelukilpailuun. Viidelle valitulle kilpailijalle maksetaan kullekin 15 000 euroa (+alv) kilpailuohjelman mukaisesta määräajassa palautetusta kilpailutyöstä. Palkkiot maksetaan Suomen Arkkitehtiliiton kautta ja SAFA perii 7 % palkinnoista kilpailusääntöjensä mukaisesti. Kilpailun tarkemmat tiedot ja aikataulu on esitetty osallistumispyynnön liitteenä olevassa kilpailuohjelman luonnoksessa.

description: THIS IS A NOTICE OF INTENT TO AWARD A SOLE SOURCE CONTRACT. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR A COMPETITIVE PROPOSAL OR QUOTATION. The Defense Logistics Agency � Energy (DLA Energy), Direct Delivery Fuels Division, hereby issues this Notice of Intent (NOI) to inform industry and prospective contractors of the Government's intent to solicit, negotiate, and award a sole-source, Firm-Fixed-Price contract with Economic Price Adjustment (FFP w/ EPA) for commercial ground fuels in accordance with the Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO), FAR Part 12 (Acquisition of Commercial Products and Commercial Services). The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) NAICS code is 324110 � Petroleum Refineries with a size standard of 1500 employees. The Product of Service Code for this requirement is 9140. This will not be a small business set aside under the Small Business Administration (SBA) size standard for this sector. The proposed contract action is being conducted under the statutory authority of 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1), as implemented by RFO FAR 6.103-1, "Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements." This is a new requirement for the procurement and direct delivery of bulk of ground fuels for Logistics Support Area (LSA) Jenkins and Prince Sultan Air Base (PSAB) in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia as follows: CLIN Fuel Product NSN Quantity Location 0001 Diesel Fuel #2 (DF2) 9140-00-286-5294 1,440,000 US Gallons LSA Jenkins, SA 0002 Diesel Fuel #2 (DF2) 9140-00-286-5294 3,240,000 US Gallons PSAB, SA 0003 Gasoline, Mid Unl (MUM) 9130-01-272-0983 2,160,000 US Gallons PSAB, SA The anticipated period of performance is from December 1, 2026 through November 30, 2029 with a six (6)-month option. The Government intends to award this requirement to Saudi Naval Support Company. Due to operational imperatives, base defense and physical security mandates, and strict installation access limitations enforced by Host Nation military authorities at LSA Jenkins and PSAB, uninterrupted fuel delivery is vital to continuous operations. Saudi Naval Support Company is currently the only vendor identified with the existing infrastructure, security clearances, vetted transportation fleets, and validated installation access credentials capable of immediate and uncompromised performance without causing unacceptable operational disruptions. This notice is not a formal request for competitive proposals or quotes. No solicitation package will be issued publicly via SAM.gov for competitive submission, and telephone inquiries will not be accepted. Unsolicited proposals or quotes received will not be accepted for award. However, all responsible sources who believe they possess the legitimate capability, infrastructure, supply chain assurance, and verified base access to perform this requirement may submit a formal Capability Statement, only if received by the closing date and time of this notice. Generic capability statements, marketing materials, or brochures will not be considered. A determination not to compete the proposed requirement based upon the responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Any response submitted must demonstrate clear, compelling, and convincing evidence that the respondent can satisfy the requirement without causing mission failure or supply interruption, and that opening competition would be advantageous to the Government. However, any responsible vendor believes they have the necessary access and capability to provide continuous, uninterrupted fuel support may submit a capability statement which shall be considered by the agency, Mandatory Submission Requirements Interested parties submitting capability statements must provide the following: Responses must include: Business name Evidence of System for Award Management (SAM) registration Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) Commercial/North Atlantic Commercial and Government Entity (CAGE/NCAGE) Code Joint Contingency Contracting System (JCCS) � Registered and Approved Demonstrated capability to meet all requirements Evidence of LSA Jenkins and PSAB Base Access approval - Verifiable documentation confirming active base access approvals, driver badging, and host nation entry permits for commercial fuel tanker operations at both LSA Jenkins and PSAB Suppliers and Transportation Letters of Commitment Certificate of Analysis/Certificate of Quality (COA/COQ) for each product � Recent (within 90 days), certified Certificate of Analysis (COA) / Certificate of Quality (COQ) verifying product conformance with applicable commercial for each fuel type. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed procurement based on the responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Information received will be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. All interested parties who are responsible, certified, and capable shall identify their interest. The DEADLINE to submit your capability statement showing your ability to meet the full scope of this requirement are due on or before November 25, 2026 by 9:00 am Eastern Standard Time (EST) by email to Regina Daniels, Contract Specialist, at regina.daniels@dla.mil and Georgia Dotson, Contracting Officer, at Georgia.Dotson@dla.mil. description: COMBINED SYNOPSIS/SOLICITATION FOR COMMERCIAL ITEMS This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial items prepared in accordance with the format in Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) subpart 12.6, "Streamlined Procedures for Evaluation and Solicitation for Commercial Items," as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; quotations are being requested, and a written solicitation document will not be issued. This solicitation is a Request for Quotations (RFQ). The solicitation document and incorporated provisions and clauses are those in effect through Federal Acquisition Circular (FAC) 2026-01 Effective: 03/13/2026. This is a Total Small Business Set-Aside in accordance with FAR 13.003 (b)(1) on a Firm-Firm Fixed-Price (FFP) basis. The associated North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) code for this procurement is 541519 with a small business size standard of $34,000,000. The associated Federal Supply Code (FSC) / Product Service Code (PSC) procurement is 7A21. The Naval Research Laboratory (NRL), located in Washington, DC, is seeking to purchase: Gigabyte Server G294-Z42-AAP2 All interested companies shall provide quotations for the following: _____________________________________________________________________________ _____________________________________________________________________________ X See specification attachment Supplies: BRAND NAME ONLY Software/Hardware/Services: This procurement is for new equipment ONLY, unless otherwise specifically stated. No remanufactured or "gray market" items are acceptable. All equipment must be covered by the manufacturer's warranty. � Vendor shall be an Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM), an OEM authorized dealer, an authorized distributor, or an authorized reseller for the proposed equipment/system such that OEM warranty and service are provided and maintained by the OEM. All software licensing, warranty, and service associated with the equipment/system shall be in accordance with the OEM terms and conditions � Offerors are required to submit documentation from the manufacturer stating that they are an authorized distributor for the specific items being procured. Note: Maintenance Renewals - The performance period for maintenance renewals, (software licenses, services, etc.), must begin on or after the date of contract award. The performance period cannot be back dated. If reinstatement fees are required, they must be listed on separate line items. Delivery Address: X U.S. Naval Research Laboratory 4555 Overlook Avenue, S.W. Bldg. 49 � Shipping/Receiving Code 3400 Washington, DC 20375 **FOB DESTINATION IS THE PREFERRED METHOD** Estimated Delivery Time: __________________ For FOB ORGIN, please provide the following information: FOB Shipping Point: _______________________ Estimated Shipping Charge: _________________ Dimensions of Package(s): ____________________ Shipping Weight: __________________________ SUBMISSION INSTRUCTIONS: All Quoters shall submit 1 (one) copy of their technical and price quote. Include your company DUNS Number and Cage Code on your quote. All quotations shall be sent via e-mail. GOVERNMENT POINT OF CONTACT Purchasing Agent Name: Elizabeth Harley Email: elizabeth.c.harley.civ@us.navy.mil Please reference this combined synopsis/solicitation number on your correspondence and in the "Subject" line of your email. ALL QUESTIONS REGARDING THE SOLICITATION SHALL BE SUBMITTED VIA EMAIL. The government intends to award a purchase order as a result of this combined synopsis/solicitation that will include the terms and conditions set forth herein. Award may be made without discussions or negotiations, therefore prospective contractors should have an active registration in the System for Award Management (SAM) database (www.sam.gov) in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Part 4.1102 and Part 52.204-7 when submitting a response to this solicitation. The Government will award a contract resulting from this solicitation to the responsible offeror whose offer conforming to the solicitation will be most advantageous to the Government, price and other factors considered. The following factors shall be used to evaluate offers: Lowest Price Technically Acceptable - Offers will be ranked lowest to highest according to price. A price analysis will be conducted to determine whether the lowest price will result from a single award or multiple awards. Based on the price analysis, the lowest price offer or multiple offers, will be forwarded to the requiring activity for technical evaluation (offer(s), in accordance with the specifications, will be deemed either technically acceptable or technically unacceptable). If the lowest price offer or offers is found technically acceptable and the pricing determined fair and reasonable by the Contracting Officer, evaluation will be deemed complete and award will be made based on the lowest price offer(s). If the lowest price offer is determined technically unacceptable, another analysis will be conducted amongst the remaining offers to determine if a single or multiple awards will provide the lowest price. The lowest price offer(s) will be sent for technical evaluation. This process is repeated in order of price until an offer or combination of offers is deemed technically acceptable and price is determined fair and reasonable. Table A-1. Technical Acceptable/Unacceptable Ratings: Rating Description Acceptable Quote meets all the minimum requirements/specifications as stated or provided in the RFQ specifications. Unacceptable Quote does not clearly meet the minimum requirements/specifications as stated or provided in the RFQ specifications. Options. When applicable, the Government will evaluate offers for award purposes by adding the total price for all options to the total price for the basic requirement. The Government may determine that an offer is unacceptable if the option prices are significantly unbalanced. Evaluation of options shall not obligate the Government to exercise the option(s). Terms and Conditions. To facilitate the award process, all quotes must include a statement regarding the terms and conditions herein as follows: "The terms and conditions in the solicitation are acceptable to be included in the award document without modification, deletion, or addition." OR "The terms and conditions in the solicitation are acceptable to be included in the award document with the exception, deletion, or addition of the following:" Exceptions. Quoter shall list exception(s) and rationale for the exception(s). Submission shall be received not later than the response date listed above. Late submissions shall be treated in accordance with the solicitation provision at FAR 52.212-1(f). E-mailed submissions are accepted and are the preferred form of submission. Receipt will be verified by the date/time stamp on fax or e-mail.

description: Kaavan tuotantojärjestelmän hankinta Kaupunkiympäristön toimiala (KYMP) on toteuttamassa Kaavan tuotantojärjestelmän hankintaa. Helsingin kaupunkiympäristön toimiala hankkii kaavan tuotantojärjestelmän, jolla pystyy tuottamaan kansallisen kaavatietomallin mukaista asema- ja yleiskaavaa ja toimittamaan ne Suomen ympäristökeskuksen ylläpitämään rakennetun ympäristön tietojärjestelmään viimeistään vuoden 2029 alusta alkaen. Hankinta sisältää ohjelmistopalvelun käyttöoikeudet, ylläpidon ja tuen sekä kiinteähintaisen käyttöönottoprojektin. Lisäksi hankinta sisältää tarvittaessa erikseen tilattavia koulutus-, jatkokehitys- ja asiantuntijapalveluja. Hankinnan tausta ja kohde on kuvattu tarkemmin liitteessä Hankinnan kohteen kuvaus.,

title: SZC CWA - Pool Bunker Construction
description: The contract will deliver a commissioned, weathertight and operational Pool Bunker above the base slab. The facility will support assembly, welding and inspection activities before modules are transferred to the Nuclear Island. The scope of works includes: • Primary steel frame and crane runway beams. • Rainscreen cladding and industrial doors, with precast cladding retained as the alternative envelope. • Five-section retractable roof. • Secondary steelwork platforms, working levels and access arrangements. • Mechanical, electrical and public health services, including local exhaust ventilation, power, lighting and controls. • Passenger and goods hoists, stair cores and roof access. • Installation and commissioning of three free-issued gantry cranes. • Tented workshop, lightning protection and earthing. • Testing, commissioning, quality records and formal handover. The base slab and the separate site non-destructive testing contract are outside this sourcing strategy. Their interfaces will be defined in the tender documents and managed through the contract programme. The key scope deliverables are: • Completed design to RIBA stage 4 and coordinated construction information. • Approved contractor programme aligned to project milestones. • Constructed and commissioned Pool Bunker, including roof, cranes, platforms, access and building services. • Completed health, safety, quality and assurance records. • Demonstrated interfaces with the base slab, utilities and non-destructive testing arrangements. • Formal handover following operational readiness review. The timescales are as follows: The Pool Bunker is required to support the planned assembly, welding and inspection of pool and tank liner modules before transfer to the Nuclear Island. The current estimated site construction period is: • 40 weeks for the preferred rainscreen and Safe RAD solution. • 46 weeks for the 275 mm precast fallback solution. The current target is for the Pool Bunker to be completed and handed over by 28 February 2028, ready to support the planned assembly, welding and inspection of pool and tank liner modules. The programme is dependent on completion of the base slab and availability of the K10 area and will be revalidated once the K10 release date is confirmed.

title: Provision of UPS - MEICA-UPS-01
description: The Subcontractor shall design, manufacture, supply, deliver, test and commission 4 No. complete UPS systems: 1 No. at Stoneleigh, 1 No. at Canley Brook and 2 No. at Burton Green. 1. Technical Requirements Each UPS shall be rated at 210 kVA, 400 V, with 4 x 60 kW power modules and N+1 hot-swappable architecture. The Subcontractor shall demonstrate that the required connected load remains supported with one power module unavailable. Requirement Stoneleigh Canley Brook Burton Green Battery sizing load 35 kW 17 kW 70 kW Connected design load 31 kW TBC 66 kW Protection breaker 100 A 100 A 250 A Separate static switch N/A N/A 400 A, 400 V Each UPS shall provide an output fault current of 987 A for 200 ms. Supplier submissions shall demonstrate compatibility with the project protection requirements. 2. Batteries Provide complete VRLA battery systems, including racks/enclosures, interconnections, isolation and protection, delivering 90 minutes' autonomy at the specified battery sizing load. Batteries shall recharge to 95% within 900 minutes. Submit sizing and recharge calculations. 3. Transformers and Ancillary Equipment Provide 250 kVA, 1:1, Dzn0 input and output isolation transformers, together with ATS, static switching and external maintenance bypass arrangements required by the approved site-specific drawings. ATS shall be 400 A, four-pole where indicated. Include all interconnecting cables, battery cables, protective devices and terminations identified as the UPS supplier's responsibility. Coordinate interfaces with incoming supplies and UPS switchboards. 4. Monitoring Provide BMS interfaces for battery DC voltage, charge percentage, battery alarms/faults and charger status/alarms. Include communications protocols, interface hardware and point schedules for the UPS, ATS and UPS switchboard, with interface testing. 5. Delivery and Coordination Scheduled UPS cabinet dimensions are 1,200 W x 1,996 H x 1,100 D mm. Confirm complete equipment footprints, weights, clearances and delivery requirements before manufacture. 6. Testing and Handover Include FAT, commissioning, SAT and resistive load bank testing, with all temporary equipment, connections and removal. Demonstrate capacity, autonomy, recharge, redundancy, transfer/bypass operation, alarms and communications. Provide evidence of fault-current performance. Submit equipment drawings, schematics, protection data, test procedures/results, commissioning records, as-built information and O&M manuals. Suppliers shall identify proposed equipment and deviations. Confirm the missing Canley Brook design load, whether Burton Green loads apply per UPS, and site-specific equipment quantities and supply boundaries before manufacture. Additional information: Please review attached schematic and narrative specification.

title: Develop Wayfinding Strategy for Mississippi Lake National Wildlife Area (MLNWA), St Clair National Wildlife Area (SCNWA) and Big Creek National Wildlife Area (BCNWA)
description: Background Canadian Wildlife Service (CWS) Ontario manages 10 National Wildlife Areas in Ontario. Two of these, Prince Edward Point National Wildlife Area (PEPNWA) and Big Creek National Wildlife Area (BCNWA) have also been designated as Connecting Canadians to Nature sites. Out of more than 60 National Wildlife Areas across the country only 10 have been designated as Connecting Canadians to Nature sites. These 10 sites as well as select few of the other NWAs are open to the public and provide opportunities for people to experience and connect with nature. CWS Ontario is working to improve accessibility and enhance visitors’ experiences at publicly accessible NWAs in Ontario. In 2025, a wayfinding strategy and upgrades to signage were completed at PEPNWA to improve accessibility for visitors. CWS Ontario is now looking to implement similar improvements at other publicly accessible NWAs in the province using guidance developed for PEPNWA. Objective Develop Wayfinding Strategy for Mississippi Lake National Wildlife Area (MLNWA), St Clair National Wildlife Area (SCNWA) and Big Creek National Wildlife Area (BCNWA) and complete signage designs as required based on outcomes of individual site visits and using guidance outlined in Design Brief (Appendix B) and Wayfinding Signage Design Intent (Appendix C) previously prepared for PEPNWA.
